name: Isomorphism
description: Fix a constant c ≥ 1. We work on a uniform deterministic word-RAM with word size Θ(log(k+n)); running times include reading the explicit input and writing the explicit output. For every k,n ≥ 1, preprocessing receives k valid attributed directed graphs G_1,...,G_k, each with at most n vertices, together with promised-correct answers A(G_1),...,A(G_k), and constructs a data structure of size polynomial in k and n. An isomorphism G ≅ H is a bijection preserving directed adjacency, integer edge weights, all vertex and edge attributes, all distinguished vertices or roles, and all encoded global parameters; vertex names are not attributes. The instance class and answer map are isomorphism-closed. A query is an arbitrary valid graph H with at most n vertices. The algorithm must output either the exact answer A(H) or the token NEW. It may output NEW only if H ≄ G_i for every i ∈ [k]; hence, if H ≅ G_i for some i, it must output A(H). This must hold even when the preprocessing instances contain duplicates or mutually isomorphic graphs. For vertex-indexed answers, reusing a stored answer requires computing, within the query-time bound, a transport map that relabels the stored answer according to the query vertices.
